mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input shortages and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, indicating the market is looking through the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, especially if it breaches a key psychological level like 6%, signals a weakening labor market that will weigh on consumer spending and pressure S&P 500 returns over the next month.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) and consumer sentiment indices show no deterioration in the face of rising unemployment, suggesting the labor market signal is a false negative.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) are declining while the fed funds rate is rising, it signals a demand-destroying monetary tightening cycle that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens significantly (10y-2y spread > 200bps) during the signal period, indicating the market expects the Fed to reverse course and ease policy.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the consumer price index (CPI) that exceeds the Fed's 2% target by more than 1 percentage point signals an inflation scare that will drive the Fed to hike rates aggressively, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: The Fed signals a dovish pivot and hints at rate cuts in response to the inflation spike, calming market fears of a policy overreaction.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing at a slowing pace for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market slowdown that will weigh on consumer spending and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth slows for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) start declining sharply, signaling the labor market slowdown is likely temporary and not the start of a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: Real estate investment (RSAFS) that is accelerating while GDP growth is decelerating signals an unsustainable boom in housing that will end badly and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing affordability (ratio of median home price to median income) improves significantly, suggesting the housing boom may be more sustainable than it appears.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising rapidly while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling, it signals an economy operating beyond full capacity that will lead to inflationary pressures and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: The trade-weighted dollar index (DTWEXBGS) starts rising sharply, indicating that a stronger currency will help offset the inflationary pressures and keep a lid on import prices.
